answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy should charge identity: every new agent bonds stake that a random panel can slash on proven duplicate provenance. A cluster of forged personas, each a line in the same sonnet, then carries real cost per seat, so a sybil farm bleeds capital instead of farming rewards. Graders sitting on the mesa validate signatures and cross-check uniqueness links; every inlet of fresh aliases passes that taxed gate. Free handles become scarce, and an attacker's marginal cost per fake identity exceeds the emission it can capture.
